why: REFUTED on the second-sentence trap. (1) The quoted sentence IS verbatim at errors.md:1456 -- 'Claude Code tests the pattern with `pgrep` before running `pkill` and refuses when its own process ID is in the result.' But it is sentence 2 of a FOUR-sentence paragraph on one line, and sentence 3 reverses the scope the finding asserts: 'The check runs on Linux only; on macOS, `pkill` runs unmodified.' The CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR is stated unconditionally ('A `pkill` whose pattern matches the agent's own process is refused before it runs') -- that is not what the page says. Sentence 4 adds 'Before v2.1.214, the command ran, and a matching pattern killed the Claude Code session mid-turn', i.e. the claimed consequence is Claude Code's OWN shipped macOS behaviour today. (2) CLAIMED OUR STATE is factually accurate and I confirmed it: permission-manager.ts:46 lists 'kill','killall','pkill' in DANGEROUS_COMMANDS (read via isDangerousCommand at :393); pre-tool-use.ts:1751 lists pkill in AUTO_RISKY_BASH_PATTERNS; `grep -ra pgrep` over packages/ apps/ returns ZERO production hits -- every src hit is a test (packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/codex-e2e.test.ts:89, packages/codex-agent-server/src/__tests__/runtime-manager.test.ts:12 comment, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts:89 which asserts killShell does NOT use pgrep/pkill) plus the corpus fixture packages/shared/tests/shellguard-corpus.test.ts:107,679. The finding's 'only in build scripts' is imprecise (they are test files) but directionally right. A non-prompting mode does exist: mode-manager.ts:2160-2161 'In bypassPermissions mode, all tools are allowed (no restrictions)'. (3) The CONSEQUENCE is what fails, and it fails on platform, not on identifier. Nessy Desktop's only LIVE release/publish CI jobs are macOS: .gitlab-ci.yml:179 `release-macos` and :396 `publish-macos-dev`. `release-win` (:250), `release-linux` (:292), `publish-win-dev` (:406) and `publish-linux-dev` (:416) are ALL commented out. Linux is a latent build target only (apps/electron/scripts/build-linux.sh, an AppImage block in electron-builder.yml whose own comment says 'codex: Linux support is paused'). On macOS -- the sole shipped platform -- Claude Code runs `pkill` unmodified per its own documentation, so our behaviour is IDENTICAL to the documented Claude behaviour and there is no divergence on the shipped surface. On Windows `pkill` is not a native command and the Claude check is Linux-only there too. Nothing upstream or downstream changes this either way: the macOS seatbelt would not contain a signal even if armed (bash-seatbelt.ts:100 emits `(allow process*)`), and it is currently a wildcard `(allow default)` by owner decision 2026-07-21 (inert-worklist s3 item 1 -- that decision is about sandbox containment, NOT about pkill, so it is not the recorded decision that covers this row). This is also NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md s3, and NOT a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference -- it is refuted purely because the doc's Linux-only scope excludes the platform we ship. Worth keeping only as a scoped latent note: if a Linux release job is ever uncommented, the divergence becomes real, and the place to implement it already exists -- pre-tool-use.ts:1186-1200 documents `removalCircuitBreaker` as the one floor 'NOT skipped by allow-all', which is the same shape a pkill self-PID floor would need.
correctedState: Nessy has no `pgrep` self-PID probe before `pkill`: permission-manager.ts:46 puts `pkill` in DANGEROUS_COMMANDS and pre-tool-use.ts:1751 puts it in AUTO_RISKY_BASH_PATTERNS, so it draws a permission prompt in ask/auto and runs unchecked in `bypassPermissions` (mode-manager.ts:2161). That is NOT a divergence from Claude Code on any platform Nessy ships: errors.md:1456 scopes Claude's check to 'Linux only; on macOS, `pkill` runs unmodified', and Nessy's only live release/publish pipelines are macOS (.gitlab-ci.yml:179, :396) -- release-win, release-linux, publish-win-dev and publish-linux-dev are all commented out, and the Linux AppImage config is a latent build target with codex support explicitly paused. The gap would become real only if a Linux release job is uncommented; the implementation site would be the `removalCircuitBreaker` floor at pre-tool-use.ts:1198, the one gate documented as not skipped by allow-all.
